incident-bot: 🔔 [AUTO] SLO burn-rate alert triggered for /v1/generate (30m window). Current burn-rate: 2.8x, error rate: 1.6% (threshold 0.5%).

incident-bot: Details: psuedo-metrics -> p50 latency +120ms, increased 5xx from 0.1% -> 1.6%, region: us-east-1. Paging rule matched: burn-rate > 2x for 15m AND error_rate > 0.5%.

Tess: oncall here, looking. @liam @pj please ack and share any running deploys?

Liam: ack. No active deploys on my side. Seeing a small surge in traffic from a partner org -> traffic spike + batching behavior odd.

PJ: ack. I'm seeing retries from edge LB -> downstream queueing on workers. Repro: tail logs show repeated 503 from runtime pool.

Maya: customer support flagged a customer-facing error page for a major partner. They reported partial failures starting ~12:04 UTC.

Tess: thanks. quick triage: 1) isolate whether it's model runtime saturation vs infra 2) check routing fallback behavior 3) find any circuit breakers triggered.

PJ: running quick ps and qstat. Kernel: lots of 'kv cache miss' and long tail token times. Suspect heavy long-context requests causing OOM thrash on some pods.

Liam: on dashboards now: per-instance GPU mem usage spikes correlated with >512 token requests. Autoscaler didn't spin new pods because burst config set to 2x but pool usage hit soft limits.

Tess: can we flip fallback to lower-cost model variant to absorb traffic? (canary policy + immediate fallback).

PJ: I pushed a routing override to route 30% of traffic to model-compact-1 for non-enterprise tokens. Command: ```/rollout override route /v1/generate -> model-compact-1 weight=30%````

incident-bot: Deploy event logged: rollout override by pj at 1923456835.

Maya: CS confirmed error rate dropped for partner after routing change, but overall burn-rate still high due to retries from queued requests.

Tess: mitigation checklist: 1) keep override for 30m 2) increase autoscaler burst to 3x temporarily 3) suppress noisy alerts for non-customer-impacting SLOs while we stabilize. Thoughts?

Liam: +1 to burst. I'll patch autoscaler: ```kubectl patch hpa inference-pool -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 60}}'``` then monitor. Doing now.

PJ: also increasing reserved KV cache to reduce eviction thrash: editing configmap kv-cache-size from 6GB -> 9GB on affected pool.

Tess: good. On alert suppression: we should avoid paging on burn-rate >2x alone while mitigation in progress, otherwise ops rotation will get flooded. Propose: change paging rule to require multi-window confirmation: burn-rate >2x in 10m AND sustained in 30m OR error_rate >1%.

Liam: agree. Create a temporary alert rule: ```alert: SLOBurnPagingProvisional expr: burn_rate > 2 and (increase_over_10m and increase_over_30m)```. Tag as `suppress-paging=true` during incident.

PJ: note: we must be careful to not suppress real customer-impact pages. Use metric customer_error_rate (only customers with SLA) for paging.

Tess: exactly. Let's use two-tier: paging if customer_error_rate > 0.4% OR (burn-rate >2x AND sustained 30m). Non-customer burn-rate alerts to create tickets but not page.

Maya: I'll update the incident summary for CS so they know who to notify if partner escalates. Also creating a public status update draft.

incident-bot: Alert status changed: suppressed paging for non-customer burn-rate at 1923456870 (reason: active mitigation).

Liam: autoscaler patched and scaling up, expected capacity in ~90s. Observing gradual drop in per-instance mem.

PJ: KV cache resized, pod restarts completed. Error rate trending down to 0.4%. Requests per second still elevated.

Tess: good. We should capture follow-ups: 1) revisit burst policy (maybe default 3x) 2) add a dashboard tile for multi-window burn-rate trend (10m/30m/1h) and customer_error_rate split by partner 3) formalize paging policy change for non-customer burn-rate.

Liam: I'll open an ops-ticket for autoscaler default change and link grafana panel. Ticket #OPS-4821.

PJ: I'll add the new dashboard panels and tag them 'oncall-slo'. ETA 3h.

Maya: I'll own the incident postmortem doc and customer impact section. Drafting now.

Tess: wrap up: keep routing override for 20 more minutes to drain. If metrics stable for 30m, rollback to normal routing and restore original alert config.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated? Current burn-rate 0.9x, error rate 0.3%. No paging triggered in last 15m.

Tess: thanks team. Postmortem owners assigned: Maya (doc + customer comms), Liam (autoscaler policy), PJ (dashboards & config), Tess (oncall review + paging policy proposal).

Maya: adding action items to the postmortem and linking to #ops-runbooks.

Liam: quick note for follow-up meeting: evaluate default autoscaler burst 2x vs 3x vs dynamic based on recent load patterns.

PJ: also propose adding a small synthetic load test that targets long-context paths to validate KV cache and autoscaler behavior pre-prod.

Tess: perfect. I'm going to close the oncall handoff in 10. Thanks all. :heart:
